controls.pre: real PowerShell server, authenticated raw WebSocket upgrade
controls.action: Open one /ws connection and concurrently GET /health.
controls.expect_ui: an unrelated lightweight endpoint stays responsive while a long-lived WS is open
controls.expect_req: GET /ws (101) + GET /health in parallel
controls.actual: wsUpgraded=false blocked=undefined healthDuringWsMs=undefined  http=503 body="websocket worker unavailable"
controls.note: FAIL here is a REAL application backend defect (R2): inline WS handling stalls the single-threaded accept loop; it is reported, never hidden

controls.action: GET /health five times.
controls.expect_req: five 200s
controls.expect_ui: n/a
controls.actual: median=41ms p95=57ms max=57ms timeouts=0
controls.note: control baseline for the during-WS comparisons

controls.action: open one /ws then GET /health.
controls.expect_req: 101 + parallel 200 /health
controls.expect_ui: n/a
controls.actual: upgrade did not complete: 503 body="websocket worker unavailable"
controls.note: cannot measure starvation without an upgrade

controls.action: hold all sockets, repeatedly GET /health and one authenticated /api/config.
controls.expect_req: all upgrades 101; /health 200 <= 1500ms; /api/config 200 <= 2500ms
controls.expect_ui: dashboard polls and button requests are not starved by many sockets
controls.actual: upgraded=0/5 healthOk=5/6 healthMax=348ms configStatus=200 configMs=32
controls.note: WS workers must not exhaust the capacity that serves HTTP

controls.action: open 9 sockets, then GET /health while saturated.
controls.expect_req: exactly 8 upgrades, excess answered 503 (not queued/hung), /health still 200
controls.expect_ui: a denied extra socket retries on the ladder instead of freezing the app
controls.actual: held=0 rejected=9 rejectStatuses=[503,503,503,503,503,503,503,503,503] firstRejectBody="websocket worker unavailable" healthDuring=200/28ms audit=true
controls.note: bounded admission: excess fails fast and never monopolizes the accept thread

controls.action: POST /api/handler-hello (a real local heartbeat-file write), then verify the file and clean up.
controls.expect_req: 200 {"ok":true} and handler-hello-last.json written while both sockets stay open
controls.expect_ui: a button/POST operation completes concurrently with live sockets
controls.actual: socketsHeld=0 post=200/87 fileWritten=true body={"ok":true}
controls.note: genuine backend mutation, not a 200-only check; test-owned files removed afterward

controls.action: upgrade and read frames, send hello.
controls.expect_req: 101 then server heartbeat/hello-ack frames
controls.expect_ui: the bridge shows genuine protocol traffic
controls.actual: upgrade failed: 503 body="websocket worker unavailable"

controls.action: send a CLOSE frame, then abruptly drop a socket and open a fresh one.
controls.expect_req: clean teardown and a successful new 101 (worker capacity released)
controls.expect_ui: the reconnect ladder restores the bridge
controls.actual: normalClose=false abruptReconnect=false
controls.note: the gate/slot must be released so reconnect succeeds

controls.pre: GHRDP_WS_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SEC=8; a socket that sends no frames
controls.action: open a silent /ws and wait for the server to close it.
controls.expect_req: server-initiated close within 14000ms
controls.expect_ui: a half-open peer is reaped, not held forever
controls.actual: expired=false waitedMs=null
controls.note: interactive sockets answer pings and are not affected; only a silent peer expires

controls.action: send a non-upgrade request to the /ws route.
controls.expect_req: an HTTP answer (400) within the bound, no hung connection
controls.expect_ui: n/a
controls.actual: result={"status":503} ms=51
controls.note: the worker preserves the original 400 path for a non-upgrade

controls.action: repeatedly open and tear down /ws workers, then sample process handles/threads and /health.
controls.expect_req: all 10 cycles upgrade, handle growth <= 200, /health still 200
controls.expect_ui: long-lived server does not accumulate runspace handles
controls.actual: okCycles=0 handles 734 -> 734 (growth=0) threads 27 -> 27 health=200/22ms
controls.note: reaper disposes PowerShell handles; sockets/streams close in worker finally
